prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

BARCELONA, Spain -- Barcelona are ready for twice world player of the year Ronaldinho to move on, said club president Joan Laporta. Ronaldinho is expected to leave Barcelona this summer after struggling for form last season. Laporta told the Catalan TV3 station that the Brazilian midfielder, who struggled with injuries and poor form last season, needed new challenges in his career. "When the wheel turns, it's normal that the key figures leave," Laporta said. "I would like Ronaldinho to be given a great send-off so that he is remembered for all he has given us and that if he didn't do any more it was because the circumstances wouldn't allow it. "Last year, we thought that it might be the year to sell him, but given his enthusiasm and the appreciation that a club like Barcelona needs to have, we decided to let him stay on. Things haven't turned out the way he wanted them to." Laporta recognized that it might not be easy to sell Ronaldinho, who suffered a series of injury and fitness problems this season and made the starting line-up in only 13 of 38 league matches. Ronaldinho last played for Barcelona in the 2-1 loss at home to Villarreal on March 9, has suffered muscle pain in his right leg been out of action ever since. AC Milan showed an interest in signing him and his brother Robert De Assis said personal terms had been agreed. But the clubs failed to reach agreement over a transfer fee. After a second successive season without a trophy Barcelona announced on May 7 that Rijkaard would leave at the end of the season and be replaced by former player Josep Guardiola. "We decided that if Frank did not continue then we would choose Guardiola because Pep possessed the necessary humility," said Laporta. "We didn't think about coaches like Mourinho or (Rafa) Benitez, who are both great coaches, but aren't right for Barcelona. So we told Rijkaard that when he left Guardiola would take his place." Barca's arch-rivals Real Madrid, who lifted another Spanish title this season, have signed their first newcomer for the next campaign by paying a reported 10 million euros ($15.5 million) for Argentine defender Ezequiel Garay from Racing Santander. Marca newspaper said the 21-year-old Argentine had signed a six-year contract. Meanwhile, reports that Real could be making a move for Manchester United's Cristiano Ronaldo were dismissed by coach Bernd Schuster. "I prefer to spend my time talking about things that have some bearing to reality," he told a press conference. Marca had reported that Real were still interested in buying Ronaldo who has put off all talk of his future until after the Champions League final.

## Football Transfer Roundup: Ronaldinho Nears Barcelona Exit as Real Madrid Target Garay and Ronaldo

Spanish football’s two giants are preparing for a significant summer of change, with Barcelona moving toward the end of Ronaldinho’s spell at Camp Nou and Real Madrid pursuing both Racing Santander defender Ezequiel Garay and Manchester United superstar Cristiano Ronaldo.

### Barcelona ready to close the Ronaldinho chapter

Ronaldinho’s five-year stay at Barcelona appears to be approaching its conclusion as the club plans a major rebuild following a second consecutive season without a trophy.

The Brazilian transformed Barcelona after arriving from Paris Saint-Germain in 2003. He helped the Catalan club win two La Liga titles and the 2006 Champions League, while his individual brilliance earned him the 2005 Ballon d’Or. By 2008, however, injuries, inconsistent form and concerns about his fitness had reduced his influence.

The arrival of Pep Guardiola as first-team coach signals a clear change of direction. Ronaldinho, along with other senior players such as Deco, is no longer considered central to the club’s plans. Barcelona are therefore prepared to listen to offers rather than retain one of their highest-paid players in a reduced role.

AC Milan have long been viewed as Ronaldinho’s preferred destination. The Italian club’s technical staff and Brazilian contingent make San Siro an obvious option, although Milan’s valuation has not always matched Barcelona’s asking price. Manchester City have also shown strong interest and could offer a considerably more lucrative financial package, while Chelsea have occasionally been linked with a move.

For Barcelona, the issue is not simply raising money. Moving Ronaldinho would give Guardiola greater freedom to reshape the team around Lionel Messi and introduce the more disciplined, high-intensity style that will define his new project.

### Real Madrid secure Ezequiel Garay

While Barcelona prepare for high-profile departures, Real Madrid have moved to strengthen their long-term defensive options by agreeing a deal for Ezequiel Garay.

The Argentine centre-back has developed into one of La Liga’s most highly regarded young defenders at Racing Santander. Comfortable in possession, strong in the air and capable of taking penalties and free kicks, Garay has attracted interest from several leading European clubs.

Madrid’s agreement is reported to be worth around €10 million. Rather than bring him straight into the first-team squad, the Spanish champions are expected to allow him to remain with Racing for another season. That arrangement gives Garay regular playing time while allowing Madrid to plan for the future of their defence.

The signing is a strategic one. Fabio Cannavaro is entering the latter stages of his career, while Christoph Metzelder has struggled with injuries. Garay offers Madrid a potential long-term partner or alternative to Pepe without requiring the club to force an immediate change at centre-back.

### Madrid intensify Cristiano Ronaldo pursuit

Garay may be the practical addition, but Cristiano Ronaldo is the player dominating Real Madrid’s summer agenda.

Ronaldo has just completed an extraordinary season with Manchester United, scoring 42 goals in all competitions and helping Sir Alex Ferguson’s side win both the Premier League and Champions League. His combination of goals, pace, technique and commercial appeal makes him Madrid’s leading transfer target.

Real president Ramón Calderón has made little secret of his admiration for the Portugal international. Reports in Spain have suggested Madrid are prepared to offer a world-record fee and an enormous salary to persuade Ronaldo to leave Old Trafford.

Manchester United’s position, however, is unequivocal: Ronaldo is not for sale. The English club have been angered by Madrid’s public courtship and have warned against attempts to unsettle a player who remains under a long-term contract. United have even raised the possibility of making a formal complaint to FIFA over Madrid’s conduct.

Ronaldo himself has kept the story alive by expressing admiration for Madrid and refusing to give an immediate, definitive commitment to United. Nevertheless, Madrid face a far more complicated negotiation than they did for Garay. United are financially strong, have no sporting reason to sell and regard Ronaldo as central to their pursuit of further trophies.

### Different strategies from Spain’s leading clubs

The developing business illustrates the contrasting situations at Barcelona and Real Madrid.

Barcelona are dismantling part of the side that reached its peak under Frank Rijkaard. Ronaldinho’s likely departure would be both symbolic and practical: the end of a celebrated era and the beginning of Guardiola’s attempt to construct a younger, more intense team.

Madrid, meanwhile, are acting from a position of strength after retaining La Liga. Garay represents long-term squad planning, while Ronaldo is the kind of global superstar the club traditionally seeks to build around.

The Garay deal is expected to proceed, although he will initially stay with Racing. The Ronaldo operation is far less certain and could dominate the entire transfer window without producing an immediate move.

### What ultimately happened

For historical context, the three stories reached different conclusions:

- **Ronaldinho left Barcelona for AC Milan in July 2008**, ending a highly influential five-year spell in Catalonia.
- **Real Madrid signed Garay in 2008**, with the defender remaining at Racing Santander on loan for the 2008–09 season before joining Madrid’s squad.
- **Cristiano Ronaldo stayed at Manchester United for one more year.** Real Madrid finally signed him in the summer of 2009 for a then-world-record fee of **£80 million**.
